corrections_after_the_first_runs: The runner loaded every transformers model with eager attention. In bfloat16 that kernel is about three times less accurate than the library's default one, which Heretic uses (probe with transformers alone: worst relative difference of the mean residual from float32 6.4e-2 with eager, 2.3e-2 with the default; under both library versions). bfloat16 and float16 runs now load the default kernel and switch to eager only for a forward pass that reads attention patterns. The bfloat16 comparison was run again from the start.

B-S4's rule for the rounded sums was corrected twice before being applied: the first wording (every element equal or one of its own bfloat16 steps apart) cannot hold for weights near zero; the second (one step at the tensor's median magnitude for every element) cannot hold for weights above the median. Final rule: |a - b| <= max(own step of a, own step of b, step at the median magnitude), and at most 1% of a tensor's elements differing.

B-S5 (the IDE's fit from Heretic's captures is bit-equal to Heretic's) is stated under the torch version of Heretic's run. The fit check asserted it under any interpreter; under another torch version it now reports the counts.

G-S9: a companion bundle reopened in a fresh root gave first-token logits that were not bit-equal (largest difference 0.372 on the Q4_0 file, 0.014 on the hybrid file). Cause: a just-committed low-rank piece held its factors as transposed views and the same piece read back from its file as contiguous tensors; the run-time overlay's product differs in the last bits between the two layouts, and the packed model can amplify that. The overlay now holds its factors contiguous; both GGUF comparisons were run again.

A replica of Heretic's randomized rank-r approximation was added after the first two bfloat16 runs, to test the explanation of the failed 4e-4 bound of B-S4 (row_normalization full). The 4e-4 bound is unchanged.
